FAST

NEWCASTLE, England, Nov 21 : Arsenal missed the chance to go eight points clear at the top of the Premier League as they were held to a 2-2 draw at Newcastle United on Saturday, with Mikel Arteta's side having to fight back from 2-1 down after a spirited display from their hosts. Arsenal looked set for an easy evening in the first half and they took the lead in the 33rd minute, Eberechi Eze latching on to a superb angled pass from Kai Havertz to sweep the ball into the net. Booed off at the break, Newcastle levelled four minutes into the second half as Martin Odegaard was robbed from a throw-in by William Osula. The Danish striker fed the ball to Harvey Barnes, who took a touch before rifling the ball past the keeper. In the 62nd minute the home side went ahead, Malick Thiaw bundling the ball into the net from close range after Arsenal failed to clear a corner. Arsenal keeper David Raya then suffered an arm injury and was replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga.

Arteta's side clawed their way back into the game in the 78th minute, Noni Madueke crowning a sweeping Arsenal attack with a left-foot shot, but keeper Lukas Hornicek should have done more to keep it out.  In a see-saw final period, neither side could find the net again, and the draw moved champions Arsenal to 28 points, six clear of Brighton & Hove Albion, who can close the gap at Hull City on Sunday.

Source: Reuters

FAST

Nov 21 : Rassie Erasmus’ watch-along in South Africa’s 20-17 loss to Ireland on Saturday provided a range of emotions but not much in the way of insight from the Springbok coach, who is serving a six-match ban for criticising match officials. Erasmus hosted a live-stream of himself watching the game from the team’s Dublin hotel, and in the week had over 100,000 people request to view the match with him on a platform he had created. He was sat in what appeared to be a conference room, drinking diet coke and getting increasingly animated as the game went on. Erasmus celebrated his team’s two tries as you would expect him too, but largely sat sullen without much in the way of expression.

Those hoping for running commentary were left disappointed, though Erasmus had to be careful not to fall foul of broadcast rights, so could not have images or sound from the game. He was seen talking animatedly to someone during the match, though with no sound it was unclear what was being said. Under the terms of his suspension, he may not have direct or indirect contact with the team during matches. Erasmus did give his thoughts at halftime, ruing the conceding of "stupid" penalties, but there was no post-game chatter as the visibly annoyed coach simply slammed the table, packed up his things and left.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Investigación sobre Nvidia en California abarca posibles infracciones del derecho penal
item.description: El fiscal general del estado, Rob Bonta, declaró el viernes que existen diversas leyes de California que podrían haberse infringido si Nvidia proporcionó información falsa al público.
item.dc:creator: Erik Larson
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — La investigación de California sobre si Nvidia Corp. vendió ilegalmente chips avanzados a China y engañó a los inversores sobre dicha conducta también está analizando posibles infracciones penales de la legislación estatal, lo que aumenta lo que está en juego para el fabricante de chips. El fiscal general del estado, Rob Bonta, declaró el viernes que existen diversas leyes de California que podrían haberse infringido si Nvidia o su antiguo consejero delegado, Jensen Huang, proporcionaran información falsa al público sobre dichas ventas. La investigación, anunciada por Bonta un día antes, se encuentra en una fase preliminar y aún no ha dado lugar a ninguna conclusión. “El marco jurídico básico que estamos analizando son las prohibiciones de la legislación de California —tanto civiles como penales— contra el engaño a los inversores y al público”, afirmó Bonta en una entrevista. “Y existen múltiples leyes diferentes que establecen prohibiciones en ese ámbito”. Nvidia no respondió de inmediato a un mensaje en el que se le solicitaban comentarios. El jueves, Bonta emitió un comunicado en el que indicaba que había enviado a Nvidia una citación judicial solicitando información relacionada con la investigación, lo que amplía las repercusiones legales de un escándalo que ha sacudido a la empresa con sede en Santa Clara (California). Dicho comunicado no mencionaba que el estado estuviera investigando posibles infracciones penales. La investigación de Bonta se desencadenó, en parte, por las revelaciones de que Huang mantuvo una relación sentimental con una presunta espía china que trabajaba en una empresa con sede en Singapur que obtenía chips avanzados de su empresa. El escándalo sumió a Nvidia en una crisis sin precedentes, lo que provocó una fuerte caída en la cotización de las acciones de la empresa y dio lugar a la destitución de Huang como director ejecutivo. El Gobierno de EE.UU. está investigando varios aspectos de la conducta de Nvidia. El presidente Donald Trump afirmó que el FBI está investigando la relación de Huang con la presunta espía, mientras que el secretario del Tesoro, Scott Bessent, señaló que la propia investigación de la empresa ayudará a determinar si esta actuó de forma “irresponsable” en lo que respecta a la venta de chips de alta gama que probablemente acabaran en China. “Creo que, a medida que la empresa lleve a cabo su investigación, descubriremos lo que realmente estaba ocurriendo”, declaró Bessent en una entrevista en Newsmax. Las revelaciones sobre Nvidia también han despertado “grandes sospechas” en la oficina de Bonta, añadió. Cualquier posible conclusión de la Fiscalía General de California de que Nvidia vendió chips ilegalmente a China y engañó al público podría, en última instancia, no tener nada que ver con la relación de Huang con una presunta espía, señaló Bonta. “Podría ser una cosa, la otra o ninguna de las dos. Por eso estamos llevando a cabo una investigación”, afirmó Bonta. “Así pues, podría haber una relación que no tuviera nada que ver con la venta de chips a China —algo que Nvidia podría haber hecho por su cuenta— o quizá no vendió ningún chip a China, independientemente de si hubo relación o no”. Si la investigación concluye que Nvidia infringió la ley, señaló Bonta, las sanciones podrían incluir una orden judicial que prohíba nuevas infracciones y la devolución de cualquier beneficio obtenido de las ventas ilegales, que podría ser considerable. Bonta añadió que, si se descubren infracciones, la investigación podría dar lugar a un proceso penal contra Nvidia, lo que también podría acarrear sanciones económicas. “Podría ser”, afirmó. “Depende de lo que se haya hecho, de lo que revelen los hechos, de quién supiera qué y cuándo, de cuál fuera la intención y el estado de ánimo, y de cuál fuera la conducta, pero podría ser posible”. Bonta señaló que la investigación podría concluir, en última instancia, que Nvidia no había vendido chips de forma ilegal a China y que no había engañado al público. Nvidia es el mayor fabricante de chips del mundo y, hasta hace poco, era la empresa que cotiza en bolsa con mayor valor de capitalización bursátil del mundo. Bajo el liderazgo de Huang, sus productos se convirtieron en un elemento fundamental para la expansión masiva de la infraestructura de inteligencia artificial. --Con la colaboración de Sam Kim.

NICE, France, Nov 21 : Champions Paris St Germain fought back after conceding early at Nice on Saturday to win 3-2 and extend their Ligue 1 lead to five points, but it came at a potentially heavy cost. France international Desire Doue injured his knee not long after he had put PSG 2-1 ahead and left the pitch in tears. "We need to wait for tomorrow's medical examinations, but it is clearly a serious injury. We could see that on television,” PSG coach Luis Enrique said. "I have spoken with him; he is in the dressing room. We need to wait for the final medical examinations to know exactly what the injury is, but it is clearly a serious one."

The visitors advanced to 26 points from 11 matches, ahead of Lille, who host Olympique Lyonnais later on Saturday. Nice went ahead after eight minutes from their first attacking move after winning possession high up the pitch, with Mohamed Amoura finishing clinically with a low shot into the far corner. Senny Mayulu equalised from a 31st-minute spot-kick, awarded for handball but only after a VAR review, and Doue netted within 60 seconds from Achraf Hakimi’s cross. Seven minutes later, however, he was carried off after he collapsed while putting weight on his right leg following what appeared to be an ordinary movement.  Ousmane Dembele came on as a substitute, returning after a month on the sidelines, to set up Ferran Torres to extend PSG’s lead in the 85th minute before Nice full back Ali Abdi pulled one back in stoppage time.

(Writing by Mark Gleeson in Cape Town; Editing by Ed Osmond)

item.title: Expresidente de Brasil, Jair Bolsonaro, ingresa a cuidados intensivos por una obstrucción intestinal
item.description: Bolsonaro se encuentra clínicamente estable, consciente y respira por sí mismo, según ha informado el hospital DF Star.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Carvalho
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — El expresidente brasileño, Jair Bolsonaro, ha sido ingresado en una unidad de cuidados intensivos debido a una obstrucción intestinal aguda, tras haber sido hospitalizado por un dolor abdominal intenso, según un comunicado emitido por el hospital este sábado. Bolsonaro se encuentra clínicamente estable, consciente y respira por sí mismo, según ha informado el hospital DF Star. Los médicos han iniciado un tratamiento que incluye hidratación, apoyo nutricional -mientras no pueda alimentarse- y la inserción de una sonda gástrica. No hay una fecha prevista para su alta. Bolsonaro fue trasladado al hospital el viernes con “fuertes dolores abdominales”, según indicó su hijo Carlos en una publicación en X. El hospital confirmó su ingreso en ese momento, señalando que se le estaban realizando pruebas. “No soy médico, pero nunca le había visto así, sobre todo durante los episodios repetidos e intensos que sufrió a lo largo de la noche”, afirmó Carlos en una nueva publicación el sábado en la que describía el estado del expresidente. El exlíder, de 71 años, ha sufrido problemas de salud recurrentes desde que fue apuñalado durante la campaña presidencial de 2018, que acabó ganando. Bolsonaro fue condenado a 27 años de prisión por conspirar para dar un golpe de Estado tras su derrota frente a Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva en las elecciones de 2022. El magistrado del Tribunal Supremo Alexandre de Moraes le permitió cumplir la condena bajo arresto domiciliario debido a sus problemas de salud. Esta semana, Moraes ha programado una votación en el Tribunal Supremo sobre la constitucionalidad de una nueva ley que podría reducir sustancialmente la condena de Bolsonaro. Está previsto que el juicio virtual comience el 4 de diciembre. El hijo mayor de Bolsonaro, Flávio, perdió frente a Lula en la segunda vuelta de las elecciones presidenciales de octubre y, posteriormente, abandonó Brasil para trasladarse a EE.UU., donde también reside su hermano Eduardo.

FAST

DUBLIN, Nov 21 : Two first-half tries from Rob Baloucoune helped a rejuvenated Ireland beat South Africa 20-17 on Saturday but a losing bonus point was enough to book the world champions a place in next weekend's Nations Championship final. With Springboks coach Rassie Erasmus watching on from his hotel serving the first of a six-match ban, Ireland dominated the first period and led the subdued Springboks 17-10 at halftime thanks to Baloucoune's tries and one from Ronan Kelleher. A Sam Prendergast penalty stretched the lead to 10 points and while a Malcolm Marx try cut it to three just before the hour, the Springboks could not breach the excellent Irish defence and fell to back-to-back defeats. "It's some effort from the lads. It's never going to be perfect against the world's best but we kept getting back into the game when we've just had something that's disappointing," said Ireland coach Andy Farrell.

"It's just shows the character of the lads. It shows us where we're at 10 months out from a World Cup." Farrell's men, who began the day with an outside shot of topping the Northern Hemisphere standings, cannot catch England but are guaranteed a top-three finish and one of the marquee games at the November 27-29 finals weekend at Twickenham. ERASMUS WATCHES ON FROM AFAR The build-up was dominated by Erasmus' ban for questioning the integrity of match officials following last week's loss to France and while some visiting fans sported masks of their suspended coach, his players' performance offered little support. They had demolished the Ireland scrum when they won in Dublin a year ago and looked ready to pick up where they left off on Saturday with a couple of early easy shoves handing Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu the opportunity to put them 3-0 up. But Ireland were a different beast this time and roared straight back, stretching the visitors with Stuart McCloskey finding Baloucoune with a fine long pass for the winger to step smartly inside for the opening try of the game on eight minutes. The in-form Ulster man was almost in again shortly after, only to lose his grip on the ball at the last second but he only had to wait a couple more minutes to notch his fourth try of the competition. While a rare obliteration of the South Africa scrum brought the biggest roar of the game and celebrations among the Irish pack who competed far better throughout, it was the Springboks' steamrolling set-piece that set up Morne van den Berg to level the scores against the run of play four minutes from the break. However, the hosts took a deserved lead into the break when Kelleher, starting at hooker with captain Dan Sheehan playing at number eight for the first time, powered over from a smart lineout maul five yards out from the Springbok line.  South Africa started the second half a little better and Canan Moodie, an early replacement for the injured Damian Willemse, was a stray boot from a brilliant finish in the corner. But they could not get any kind of flow into their game, even after the deployment of their 'Bomb Squad' from the bench helped lead to the converted Marx try that set up the tight finish. Ireland crucially remained on the front foot and stood up to some late pressure to the dismay of Erasmus, who smashed the table at full time and shouted at a TV during a live online watch party he was hosting four kilometres away at the team hotel. "We never promise we're going to win every game, but we know as a group that we can definitely be better," said South Africa captain Siya Kolisi. "I don't question the boys' effort, I don't question their mindset and wanting to win all the time but it's just finding plans to be better and executing better... There's a lot that we know that we need to fix, but we do know how to fix it."

Source: Reuters

FAST

Nov 21 : World chess governing body FIDE referred Magnus Carlsen to its Ethics and Disciplinary Commission (EDC) after the Norwegian forfeited three games during a pilot event for the Total Chess World Championship Tour in Budapest, the federation said on Saturday. In a statement, FIDE criticised Carlsen for missing three scheduled games against Vladislav Artemiev while their 17th-place playoff was still undecided. Carlsen forfeited both rapid games on the opening day of the match and a fast classic game on day two before prevailing in an armageddon tie-break. “Given GM Carlsen’s stature and his significant role in promoting chess, such actions are particularly concerning, as they may damage the reputation of competitions and demonstrate a lack of respect for opponents, spectators, and tournament partners,” FIDE said.

LONDON, Nov 21 : Xabi Alonso's Chelsea players looked brittle, unsure and devoid of ideas as they were crushed 4-1 by visitors Leeds United in the Premier League on Saturday. A first win at Stamford Bridge for the Yorkshire side since 1999 lifted them into sixth place in the table as Chelsea, who have now lost three games in a row, tumbled from fifth to eighth. It was also the second straight home defeat for the Blues who were outgunned 2-0 before the international break by fierce London rivals Tottenham Hotspur, then succumbed to a colourless 1-0 defeat at Sunderland. Leeds more than deserved their comprehensive victory. Although Chelsea went ahead through a powerful 25th-minute finish from Emmanuel Emegha, making his first start for Chelsea, it was against the run of play.

The lead lasted barely three minutes before Noah Okafor swerved round three defenders to send his shot into the bottom corner of Emilio Martinez's net. "Today I felt we were in a fragile moment mentally," Alonso told reporters. "It went wrong after the equaliser. We lost completely the momentum," the former Spain international added. "From that moment they start believing and we start not believing." Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin scored from the spot in the 53rd minute after a long VAR check backed referee Michael Oliver in giving a handball decision against Morgan Rogers. Okafor, completely unmarked, hooked the ball into Martinez's net in the 58th minute and Brenden Aaronson scored in added time. It had started as an untidy game full of niggly fouls but with none of the violence of the infamously bad-temperered 20th century clashes between the sides, culminating in the 1970 FA Cup final won in a replay by Chelsea on a mud pitch and dubbed the most brutal game in English domestic football.It was Leeds who showed the greater hunger, motivation and positive aggression on Saturday, forcing Chelsea's fragile defence, who have now shipped 20 goals this season, on to the back foot. "We were from the first minute to the last the better side," Leeds manager Daniel Farke said. "We have shown the desire to work and the hunger to dig in." Calvert-Lewin missed a hatful of early chances and Leeds finished with 21 shots to Chelsea's 14. "We know what the history of this game is like and what the fans expect - we know they have wanted a win here for a long time. It's right we can enjoy this performance," Leeds captain and former Chelsea midfielder Ethan Ampadu told BBC TV.

item.title: Terremoto en Perú de magnitud 6,7 grados ha dejado 15 heridos
item.description: Perú se vio sacudido por un potente terremoto a última hora del viernes que dejó más de una docena de heridos y causó daños en más de 120 viviendas.
item.dc:creator: Carla Samon Ros
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — Perú se vio sacudido por un potente terremoto a última hora del viernes que dejó más de una docena de heridos, causó daños en más de 120 viviendas y provocó cortes de electricidad en un distrito del centro del país. El sismo de magnitud 6,7 grados, se produjo poco después de las 19:00 horas, hora local, a una profundidad de más de 129 kilómetros, con epicentro en la región andina de Junín, según el Instituto Geofísico del Estado de Perú. El temblor se sintió en varias partes del país, incluida la capital, Lima. Las autoridades de emergencia informaron de que 15 personas resultaron heridas, 11 de ellas en la zona del epicentro, mientras que 127 hogares se vieron afectados, cuatro de los cuales se consideraron inhabitables. Se registraron dos réplicas de menor intensidad en Junín, según el Centro Sismológico Nacional. Un hospital y algunas viviendas en las zonas cercanas al epicentro del terremoto sufrieron daños leves, según declaró el sábado el ministro de Defensa, Rafael Belaunde, a los medios de comunicación locales. Asimismo, se produjo un corte de electricidad en una provincia y dos carreteras resultaron afectadas, añadió. El terremoto también se sintió en Bogotá y en otras partes de Colombia, según los medios de comunicación locales. --Con la colaboración de Nicolle Yapur.

LONDON, Nov 21 : Tottenham Hotspur teenager Luca Williams-Barnett became the club's youngest Premier League scorer since Gareth Bale as he marked his first top-flight start with the opening goal in a 2-0 win over Ipswich Town on Saturday. Williams-Barnett, who turned 18 last month, stabbed home Pedro Porro's cross in the 15th minute and helped set up his side's second for Dominic Solanke with a jinking run. It was only a fifth Tottenham appearance for the England junior international but the winger rewarded manager Roberto de Zerbi's faith. "Luca was magnificent today. We see him in training every day, we know what a player he is. He's such a talent, honestly," Solanke said.

"To see him come in and do that on his first Premier League start is crazy. We'll be celebrating with him today. He can bring so much for us. "He's very dedicated and so brave on the ball which is great, in his position I think you need that. We can see so much in him. It's exciting times for all of us, especially him." Bale was also 18 when he scored his first league goal for Tottenham in 2007. The club's youngest Premier League scorer was Andy Turner aged 17 in 1992. Welsh winger Bale went on to become a Tottenham great and a five-times Champions League winner with Real Madrid. Tottenham's fans are clearly excited to see a young talent shining so bright and they gave Williams-Barnett a standing ovation when he was substituted after 64 minutes. "Honestly, he's just an incredible football player. I hope he keeps doing what he's doing," Tottenham defender Destiny Udogie said. "Doing what he is doing in training and in the game is just unbelievable." Tottenham's victory, their fourth in the last five league games after failing to win any of the opening five, moved De Zerbi's side into ninth spot in the table.

LONDON, Nov 21 : New Zealand coach Dave Rennie said he took responsibility for the All Blacks' abject defeat to England on Saturday, with back-to-back poor performances putting him under pressure ahead of one last game in a disappointing 2026. After last week's surprise loss to Wales, New Zealand's first in 73 years, Rennie said that "we let our country down" and he admitted their display at Twickenham was even worse. Rennie said New Zealand were "miles off" England in their fifth defeat of 2026, marking only the third time the All Blacks have lost that many games in a year. "I'd say if you look at last week's performance, the only thing we lacked was finishing," Rennie told reporters.

"Outside of that there was a lot of good footy played, but we were miles off tonight, so it's clearly not where we want to be. I mentioned last week that I felt we let the country down and it was a way worse performance tonight, I felt." Last year, New Zealand's Grand Slam hopes were ended at Twickenham and then-coach Scott Robertson only took charge of one more game before he stood down. With New Zealand having one game left in 2026, Rennie was asked about the parallels with his predecessor and whether he felt under pressure. "As head coach, you're responsible for all the results," he said. "I'm not going to hide from the fact that we weren't good enough tonight and I'm a big part of that." Rennie was, however, sure he would be able to pick up his players, saying: "We had a bit of practice last week. Look, it's a really proud group, we're all incredibly disappointed. So we'll want to make amends for that. "I think getting the guys back up for one last crack won't be difficult."

item.title: Wall Street se pregunta qué puede salvar el mercado de la IA tras la caída de Anthropic
item.description: Ha sido un mes difícil para el mercado bursátil, sacudido por dos golpes consecutivos: la sorprendente destitución de Jensen Huang de Nvidia y la victoria decisiva de los demócratas en el Congreso.
item.dc:creator: Jeran Wittenstein, Ryan Vlastelica
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — Ha sido un mes difícil para el mercado bursátil, sacudido por dos golpes consecutivos: la sorprendente destitución de Jensen Huang de Nvidia Corp. y la victoria decisiva de los demócratas en las elecciones de mitad de legislatura. Se suponía que la salida a bolsa de Anthropic PBC, que ha batido récords esta semana, aportaría cierto alivio y cambiaría el estado de ánimo. No fue así. Por el contrario, suscitó más interrogantes sobre el sector de la inteligencia artificial, que atraviesa dificultades, y las acciones tecnológicas continuaron registrando ventas masivas, lideradas por los fabricantes de chips, lo que provocó que el índice Nasdaq 100 se desplomara un 10% durante la semana, su peor rendimiento desde que estalló la pandemia de la COVID-19 en marzo de 2020. Ahora, con escasos catalizadores positivos y una serie de riesgos evidentes en el horizonte -a empezar por la subida de tasas de interés que se espera aplique la Reserva Federal el próximo mes-, Wall Street se pregunta qué impulsará a las acciones a volver a subir. En lugar de encontrar motivos para comprar, los inversores no dejan de descubrir razones para vender, ya que, al parecer, cada dos por tres, los titulares de las noticias -desde la suspensión de los vuelos hasta los ataques informáticos- alimentan la sospecha de que la tecnología no se está adaptando a los riesgos que plantea la IA. “El mercado se encuentra en un limbo, especialmente en lo que respecta a la tecnología y la IA”, afirmó Paul Nolte, estratega de mercado y gestor senior de patrimonio en Murphy & Sylvest Wealth Management. “Hay que prepararse y esperar un periodo de volatilidad y riesgo bajista”. La operación de Anthropic podría marcar el fin del “trade” de la IA, escribió el jueves Anna Wong, economista de Bloomberg Economics, en un informe. Las cuentas de la empresa muestran un debilitamiento del poder de fijación de precios en el sector de la inteligencia de vanguardia, señaló, lo que significa que, a pesar de toda la demanda de servicios de IA, los principales proveedores están teniendo dificultades para conseguir que los clientes paguen lo suficiente como para justificar su inversión. Por supuesto, aisladamente, la salida a bolsa de Anthropic salió bien. Se fijó un precio por encima del rango previsto y, al combinarse con una colocación privada de acciones independiente, la empresa recaudó la mayor cantidad de efectivo jamás obtenida en una nueva emisión, superando la operación de SpaceX en junio. Las acciones incluso se dispararon al inicio de la cotización. Sin embargo, se estabilizaron rápidamente y luego comenzaron a retroceder. Al cierre del viernes, se situaban a menos de US$6 de su precio de salida a bolsa. El problema más grave es que esto provocó más ventas en lugar de dar a los inversores un motivo para comprar. Al cierre del viernes, el Nasdaq 100 se encontraba al borde de un mercado bajista -definido como una caída del 20% respecto a un máximo reciente-, mientras que el índice S&P 500 había entrado en una fase de corrección tras caer un 12% desde su récord de octubre. Todas esas ventas pusieron de manifiesto la magnitud de las dudas que rodean a la IA, tras más de cuatro años de un mercado alcista impulsado por enormes apuestas por esta tecnología. “Existía la esperanza de que la salida a bolsa de Anthropic proporcionara un impulso sostenido, pero la evolución de la cotización es indicativa de las preocupaciones más generales que rodean a la IA”, afirmó Jim Baird, director de inversiones de Plante Moran Financial Advisors. “Anthropic salió a bolsa en un momento de escepticismo generalizado en torno a este sector, y existen muchas dudas sobre su capacidad a corto plazo para estar a la altura de unas expectativas cada vez más elevadas”. Las victorias demócratas en las elecciones de mitad de legislatura han aumentado el riesgo de que se ralentice la construcción de centros de datos, ya que muchos de los candidatos del partido se presentaron con la promesa de frenar su desarrollo. Mientras tanto, el riesgo de una subida de los tipos de interés eleva el coste del capital, ya que los grandes promotores de centros de datos recurren cada vez más a los mercados de crédito para obtener financiación. “Gran parte del crecimiento de la IA depende de cómo y si las empresas pueden financiar sus necesidades de capital”, afirmó Malcolm Polley, director de análisis estratégico de mercado de Stratos Investment Management, que cuenta con US$3.600 millones en activos. “¿Tendrán que financiarlo a través de los mercados de capital o de deuda? Hasta que no conozcamos el coste del capital, no podremos valorar adecuadamente el activo, y si el coste del capital sigue subiendo, las valoraciones tendrán que bajar". Pero es el caos en Nvidia lo que realmente ha asustado a los inversores. La empresa destituyó a Huang el 12 de noviembre después de que este admitiera haber mantenido una relación con una mujer sospechosa de espiar para China, y desde entonces las acciones han entrado en picado. Ni siquiera un sólido informe de resultados, que incluía una previsión de ingresos al alza para el próximo ejercicio fiscal y una autorización para la recompra de acciones por valor de US$150.000 millones, logró frenar las ventas, ya que seguía sin resolverse la cuestión de quién será el sustituto definitivo de Huang. Las acciones de Nvidia se desplomaron un 23% esta semana, su peor rendimiento desde 2008. La cotización ha caído un 48% desde el máximo histórico alcanzado el 6 de octubre. La agitación parecía abrir oportunidades para los competidores de Nvidia, entre ellos el fabricante de chips Advanced Micro Devices Inc. Sin embargo, esa apuesta sufrió un revés el jueves, cuando un vendedor en corto planteó dudas sobre el negocio de AMD en China, que podría verse perjudicado por nuevas restricciones estadounidenses a la exportación de chips. Las acciones se desplomaron un 20% en las dos últimas sesiones de la semana. En términos más generales, es la sostenibilidad de los cientos de miles de millones de dólares que se están invirtiendo para ampliar la potencia informática lo que está impulsando la ola de ventas. Ese gasto ha impulsado los beneficios de las empresas de todo el ecosistema de la inteligencia artificial, desde fabricantes de chips y de equipos de red hasta proveedores de electricidad y empresas industriales. No obstante, los inversores se muestran cada vez más escépticos respecto a que esta situación pueda perdurar. Este rápido cambio de la codicia al miedo se aprecia mejor en la cotización de las acciones de semiconductores este año. Históricamente, el sector de los chips es cíclico: sube con la demanda y luego cae a medida que esta se disipa. No obstante, se creía que esta historia se reescribiría, ya que los años de demanda impulsada por la IA romperían el ciclo. El índice de semiconductores de la Bolsa de Filadelfia se duplicó con creces en la primera mitad del año gracias a esa apuesta. Sin embargo, ha perdido un 41% en la segunda mitad, a medida que los inversores se replantean esas posiciones. Las acciones de memoria y almacenamiento, que también se han beneficiado en gran medida del gasto en inteligencia artificial, han sido de las más afectadas en los últimos meses. Sandisk Corp. lideró el S&P 500 durante los primeros seis meses del año, con una subida del 857%. Es la acción con peor rendimiento del índice en el segundo semestre, con una caída del 72%. Western Digital Corp. se ha desplomado más de un 65% desde su récord de junio, mientras que Micron Technology Inc. ha bajado más de un 50% desde su máximo histórico. Por supuesto, sigue habiendo cierto optimismo en Wall Street. En concreto, se espera que la ola de ventas esté llegando a su fin, ya que los inversores han aprovechado la oportunidad para reducir el riesgo, según Brian Smedley, director de inversiones y responsable de Cynosure Strategies, la división de fondos de cobertura del Grupo Cynosure. “Creo que los inversores recuperarán la confianza en que la demanda de IA sigue siendo excepcionalmente fuerte y que los principales actores -entre ellos, Anthropic- seguirán teniendo unas perspectivas de crecimiento muy sólidas”, afirmó. “El mercado se ha excedido a la baja, al igual que se excedió al alza a principios de este año”. En lo que sí coinciden los inversores es en que la salida a bolsa de Anthropic aportará un nuevo nivel de visibilidad al negocio de la venta de servicios de IA. “Ha sido difícil hacerse una idea real de la demanda de IA, y Anthropic es la respuesta a esa pregunta”, señaló Marta Norton, estratega jefe de inversiones de Empower. “Sabremos más sobre el potencial alcista de la IA, tanto en términos de demanda como de rentabilidad, al mismo tiempo que obtendremos una visión más clara de lo desmesuradamente cara que resulta”. Mientras tanto, los estrategas aconsejan a sus clientes que se mantengan flexibles. “Es difícil predecir qué podría ser necesario para impulsar las ganancias tras esta semana”, señaló Mark Luschini, estratega jefe de mercados de Janney Montgomery Scott. “Quiero ver si esta ola de ventas se agrava y se convierte en algo más grave. Nos encontramos en una situación de sobreventa, pero no muy profunda. Podríamos caer aún más. Quiero ver una estabilización antes de comprometerme firmemente”.

England's record win over All Blacks should not be our ceiling, says Itoje

Rugby Union - Nations Championship - England v New Zealand - Allianz Stadium, Twickenham, Britain - November 21, 2026 England's Maro Itoje celebrates lifting the Hillary Shield after the match Action Images via Reuters/Peter Cziborra

Rugby Union - Nations Championship - England v New Zealand - Allianz Stadium, Twickenham, Britain - November 21, 2026 England's Maro Itoje in action New Zealand's Scott Barrett Action Images via Reuters/Peter Cziborra

FAST

LONDON, Nov 21 : England captain Maro Itoje was delighted with a record 37-12 victory over New Zealand on Saturday, but is determined that his side keeps improving. After four victories in a row over Fiji, Argentina, Australia and Japan, England were braced for a much sterner test against the All Blacks, who were hurting from a shock loss to Wales. But England demolished New Zealand, racing into an early lead and ultimately winning at a canter to record back-to-back victories over the All Blacks for the first time since 2003. "I thought we took a step forward today," Itoje told reporters. "I thought we took advantage of the opportunity we had, but ... we don't want this to be our ceiling, we don't want this to be as good as it gets for England.

"We want to push, we want to get better. We have an amazing opportunity next week, however the chips fall to do that." ENGLAND HONOUR MOODY Former England captain Lewis Moody, who was diagnosed with motor neurone disease last year, lined up with the England players for the pre-match haka, as England reprised their V formation from last year's victory. "Lewis is such an inspirational man, he was an inspirational player and, given his diagnosis, the players jumped at the opportunity to support him," Itoje said. "I think he and his family gave us that extra lift today. He came to spend some time with us yesterday, he presented us our shirts for today's game. "He addressed us and there's no doubt that his presence, him joining us for the haka, him spending time with us, gave us an extra lift." Itoje, though, played down the impact of how England responded to the haka. "The most important thing is how you start the game against New Zealand," he said. "You can do whatever you want. There are teams historically who've done different things, different formations. "It's important, but the most important thing is how you start the game. I wouldn't pay too much attention to whatever anyone does to respond to the haka."

Source: Reuters

item.title: RBI Guv opens financial inclusion camp in Maharashtra, focuses on re-KYC
item.description: Malhotra also visited stalls set up by banks, Centres for Financial Literacy (CFLs) and self-help groups (SHGs), and interacted with their representatives ...
item.dc:creator: Anjali Kumari
item.content:encoded: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Governor Sanjay Malhotra on Saturday inaugurated a special financial inclusion camp at Vaksai in Maharashtra's Maval taluka, with a focus on re-KYC of bank accounts and expanding access to banking services. The camp, organised by Bank of Maharashtra on November 21 as part of the nationwide financial inclusion campaign, facilitated re-KYC of bank accounts, access to banking services and enrolment under social security schemes. Malhotra also visited stalls set up by banks, Centres for Financial Literacy (CFLs) and self-help groups (SHGs), and interacted with their representatives. The camp was attended by the managing directors and chief executive officers of Bank of Maharashtra and Bank of India, a deputy managing director of State Bank of India, and senior officials of other banks.

item.title: New to The Street Show #781 Premieres Tonight on Bloomberg Television with Roadzen, Robo.ai, PureCipher and American Fusion
item.description: Jane King hosts conversations on AI-powered insurance, UAE industrial AI, AI safety and fusion energy, airing at 6:30 p.m. ET across the United States, Latin America, MENA and Southeast AsiaNEW YORK ...
item.content:encoded:
News / ACCESS Newswire / New to The Street Show #781 Premieres Tonight on Bloomberg Television with Roadzen, Robo.ai, PureCipher and American Fusion

New to The Street Show #781 Premieres Tonight on Bloomberg Television with Roadzen, Robo.ai, PureCipher and American Fusion 7 min read

RDZN AIIO AMFN SSGC Jane King hosts conversations on AI-powered insurance, UAE industrial AI, AI safety and fusion energy, airing at 6:30 p.m. ET across the United States, Latin America, MENA and Southeast Asia NEW YORK CITY, NY / ACCESS Newswire / November 21, 2026 / Artificial intelligence is moving out of the lab and into the real economy. Car makers and fleets are putting it to work on insurance and claims. Sovereign investors are building it into local industry. Robots and autonomous agents are starting to act on our behalf, raising a hard question about who keeps them in check. And the data centers that power it all need a new source of clean, around-the-clock energy. Tonight, New to The Street brings leaders working on each of those challenges to a global business audience as Show #781 premieres at 6:30 p.m. ET on Bloomberg Television as sponsored programming, with distribution across the United States, Latin America, the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) and Southeast Asia. Hosted by Jane King, Show #781 features executive conversations with: Rohan Malhotra , Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Roadzen Inc. RDZN Adrian Wong , Chief Financial Officer of Robo.ai Inc. AIIO Wendy Chin , Chief Executive Officer and Founder of PureCipher Inc. Brent Nelson , Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of American Fusion Inc. AMFN "Show #781 is about AI growing up," said Vince Caruso, Co-Founder and CEO of New to The Street. "An insurance technology company that just posted its first positive adjusted EBITDA quarter. A UAE-based, Nasdaq-listed group turning AI into revenue and local industry. A founder who has spent four years building the safety layer AI will need. And a fusion company working to power it all. These are the stories our audience in every region tunes in for. No politics. No current events. Opportunities To Consider™." INSIDE SHOW #781 Roadzen Inc. RDZN : A Milestone Quarter and the Road to Cash Flow Breakeven Founder and CEO Rohan Malhotra returns to walk Jane King through what he calls "a quarter we've been building up for a couple of years." Roadzen, a global AI company at the convergence of insurance and mobility, recently reported record second fiscal quarter revenue of $17.6 million, its third consecutive record quarter, and the first positive Adjusted EBITDA quarter in its history. Malhotra says Roadzen's insurer, car maker and fleet clients "are adopting AI very rapidly," and that the company is seeing "an acceleration on almost all aspects of our business." With costs largely fixed, he explains, "every new dollar of revenue should contribute to a better margin," and a growing mix of higher-margin U.S. business, together with a pending acquisition in Europe, should help margins continue to expand. Having reached Adjusted EBITDA breakeven, Malhotra says the next milestone is clear: "The second milestone for us over the next year is to get to cash flow breakeven." He also addresses the balance sheet directly, describing the company's work to retire inherited liabilities at a discount and to bring in new equity on the best possible terms. Learn more at roadzen.ai. Robo.ai Inc. AIIO : Turning UAE AI Ambition into Revenue Chief Financial Officer Adrian Wong describes Robo.ai as "a UAE-based diversified technology company serving critical infrastructure industries," and walks Jane King through how each of its three business units makes money: Quantum Core Capital (QC Capital) , acquired in June and now fully integrated, provides AI-agent-based operations management and delivery optimization for e-commerce companies and is the group's main revenue driver. Neurovia AI focuses on AI data processing and visual data compression. Having completed validation, the unit is now integrating with government and enterprise customers. ALIF Holding , the group's industrial arm, is building local manufacturing and systems integration capability in the UAE. It was recently awarded its first contract by a federal government-owned company. Wong says that, based on management accounts, revenue from June through October surpassed $380 million, and that the company is targeting up to $600 million for the full year. He also discusses the recent appointment of W Motors founder Ralph R. Debbas as Group President. "Ralph is a builder," Wong said, noting that Debbas brings deep local industrial experience as the group moves its products "from the drawing board to actual delivery" for clients. On the AI data center build-out, Wong sees "a huge opportunity," with Neurovia working to solve "one of the largest bottlenecks," which he calls "the visual data wall." Neurovia's goal is to store more visual data on the same servers, or the same data with less compute, power, water and land. Learn more at roboai.group. PureCipher Inc.: Keeping AI "on the Human Side" Wendy Chin, CEO and Founder of PureCipher, joins Jane King in New York to explain why she left a career that began at Bell Labs, and later took her to Asia-Pacific division leadership, to focus on AI security and safety. "PureCipher's mission is to ensure AI is on the human side," she said. Chin compares technology to a knife that "cuts both ways." "With great power comes great responsibility," she said. "And AI, in my view, is that power." She started building PureCipher's security and safety technology four years ago, before the launch of ChatGPT, and says the market has now caught up: "We are now just on time to talk about AI safety." As AI moves into robots, drones and cars, Chin explains why fixed, pre-built guardrails are not enough. Once an AI system is given a mission, she notes, it looks for the fastest way to achieve it. She says PureCipher is building real-time, intent-specific guardrails so that AI agents and physical AI systems follow human intent and stay within clear boundaries, and that the company is in discussions with a large company about applying this capability to physical AI. "I want AI to serve humanity," she said, "not the other way around." Learn more at purecipher.com. American Fusion Inc. AMFN : Independent Review, a New Texas Campus and the Path to Uplisting Chairman and CEO Brent Nelson updates Jane King on American Fusion's Texatron™ fusion engine. Nelson says an independent third-party reviewer recently completed an on-site evaluation of the technology. "The draft highlights look good so far," he said, adding that the company hopes the final report will confirm "that we're on the right track." Nelson says his priorities for the next six months include filing the company's quarterly report, closing on its North Texas "Ranch" facility, which American Fusion expected to complete by Thanksgiving, and building its own testing bunker there. The company is also moving into new lab and office space. "We're still operating and testing the Texatron on a daily basis," he said, "and our data is getting better." He says American Fusion has 10 to 11 data center proposals outstanding, with a combined value he puts "in the billions of dollars," and that its patent program remains active. On the capital markets, Nelson says the company is evaluating four or five of the top proposals from roughly 15 it has received from prospective financial partners, as it works toward an uplisting to the Texas Stock Exchange, Nasdaq or the New York Stock Exchange, a move he hopes to make "in the next six months or so." Learn more at americanfusionenergy.com. FEATURED COMMERCIALS SafeSpace Global Corporation SSGC : An AI-powered safety and security platform designed to help protect the vulnerable in schools, senior care, addiction treatment, correctional facilities and houses of worship. "Smarter technology, faster response, safer spaces." Big Sky Industrial BSIN : Advancing helium production, carbon management and strategic energy infrastructure through its flagship Big Sky Carbon Hub, targeting demand from AI, semiconductors, healthcare and aerospace. T-REX Acquisition Corp. TRXA : Completed a strategic refinancing of its Orofino, Idaho data center and added a new appointment to its board of directors. Acurx Pharmaceuticals, Inc. ACXP : Developing what could be the first new class of antibiotics in nearly 40 years, with the FDA agreeing to consider a future application for lead drug ibezapolstat based on two planned trials, Pathfinder and Aspire. HOW TO WATCH Bloomberg Television: Tonight, Saturday, November 21, 2026, at 6:30 p.m. ET, with distribution across the United States, Latin America, MENA and Southeast Asia New to The Street TV on YouTube (5.48M+ subscribers): https://www.youtube.com/@NewtoTheStreetTV NewsOut on YouTube (1.24M+ subscribers): https://www.youtube.com/@NewsOutChannel Following the broadcast, every segment will be distributed across the New to The Street TV and NewsOut YouTube channels, which together have more than 6.7 million subscribers. NEW TO THE STREET'S YOUTUBE AUDIENCE As of November 21, 2026, New to The Street TV (5.48M+ subscribers) and NewsOut (1.24M+ subscribers) together reach 6.72M+ YouTube subscribers. Among the financial and business media channels compared below, only The Wall Street Journal (6.74M) has more. On its own, New to The Street TV is ahead of Reuters (4.39M), CNBC (4.18M), CNBC Television (3.42M), Fox Business (3.40M) and Bloomberg Television (3.35M). Source: public YouTube channel pages as of November 21, 2026, using YouTube's rounded figures. New to The Street TV and NewsOut figures come from SocialCounts live counts, rounded down: New to The Street TV (5,482,280) and NewsOut (1,245,328). The comparison channels are The Wall Street Journal, Reuters, CNBC, CNBC Television, Fox Business, Bloomberg Television, Yahoo Finance, Cheddar, Schwab Network, Benzinga, Investor's Business Daily, TheStreet, New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq. MEET THE COMPANIES 2027: NEW YORK, ATLANTIC CITY AND LAS VEGAS New to The Street's Meet The Companies tour brings presenting companies face to face with family offices, accredited investors and high-net-worth individuals in three cities in 2027. Every presentation is filmed and distributed across New to The Street's U.S., Latin America, MENA and Southeast Asia platforms and its 6.7M+ subscriber YouTube network, so each company reaches a guaranteed audience well beyond the room. No vendor pitches. New York: Thursday, January 7, 2027, at The Hudson Yards Penthouse, 455 Tenth Avenue PH, New York, NY 10018, the week before the Needham Growth Conference, with a cocktail reception on Wednesday, January 6 Atlantic City: Thursday, January 28, 2027 Las Vegas: June 17-18, 2027 Each event hosts up to 20 presenting companies, with 20-minute slots that include a 15-minute presentation and Q&A. For Atlantic City and Las Vegas presenters, New to The Street pays for your stay. Confirmed New York Presenters: Glint (glintpay.com); TMC the metals company Inc. TMC ; American Fusion Inc. AMFN ; Big Sky Industrial BSIN ; T-REX Acquisition Corp. TRXA ; Stewards, Inc. SWRD ; Roadzen Inc. RDZN ; Smile Design Manhattan Additional presenters will be announced. Accredited investors only. Apply to attend: John@NewtoTheStreet.com. Companies interested in a presenting slot can contact John Battenfield at John@NewtoTheStreet.com. ABOUT NEW TO THE STREET Founded in 2009, New to The Street is a sponsored and syndicated business television platform serving public companies, emerging-growth businesses and companies preparing to enter the public markets. Co-founded and led by CEO Vince Caruso, New to The Street combines weekly Bloomberg Television broadcasts across the United States, Latin America, MENA and Southeast Asia with long-form executive interviews, television commercials, earned media, social-media distribution, NewsOut video press-release coverage, accredited-investor events and premium outdoor advertising, including Times Square billboards. The platform has worked with more than 200 public companies. No politics. No current events. Opportunities To Consider™. SOURCE: New to The Street

item.title: Mercado energético europeo está lanzando una señal de alerta a su economía
item.description: Los costos de la electricidad, que se mantienen persistentemente elevados, amenazan la producción industrial en toda Europa.
item.dc:creator: Eva Brendel
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — En una fábrica de Alemania, cada vez son más frecuentes los momentos en los que resulta sencillamente demasiado caro producir acero. El director de la planta, Uwe Reinecke, recibe dos correos electrónicos al día con los precios de la electricidad del día siguiente, lo que le ayuda a determinar, casi hora a hora, cuándo la planta puede permitirse funcionar. El aumento vertiginoso de los costos energéticos ha obligado en repetidas ocasiones a la planta, propiedad del grupo italiano Feralpi, a detener la producción este otoño, a pesar de tener pedidos pendientes. Esta difícil situación pone de manifiesto una cruda realidad: la segunda gran crisis energética de Europa en menos de cinco años ya se está afianzando en los mercados mayoristas. Los contratos de electricidad para cada uno de los próximos tres meses se negocian en torno a los €200 por megavatio-hora, aproximadamente el doble de los niveles del invierno pasado. El principal culpable es de sobra conocido: el aumento vertiginoso de los precios del gas natural. Las consecuencias van mucho más allá de una acería alemana. Los costos de la electricidad, que se mantienen persistentemente elevados, amenazan la producción industrial en toda Europa, corren el riesgo de agravar las presiones inflacionistas y podrían acabar repercutiendo en las facturas de los hogares. También corren el riesgo de erosionar aún más la competitividad de la región y poner a prueba una economía que, hasta ahora, ha demostrado ser sorprendentemente resistente a la última crisis energética. Muchos fabricantes con un elevado consumo energético adquieren una gran parte de su electricidad en el mercado al contado, lo que les deja inmediatamente expuestos cuando los precios suben. La planta de Feralpi se encuentra entre ellas, ya que depende de la electricidad para alimentar su horno y compra gran parte de sus necesidades poco antes de la entrega. “La subida actual de los precios es considerablemente más pronunciada que el aumento que hemos venido observando desde el verano, y eso nos está causando enormes dificultades”, afirmó Reinecke. Los precios al por mayor son los que pagan las empresas de suministro eléctrico y los consumidores industriales al adquirir electricidad en el mercado, con contratos que abarcan desde el suministro para el día siguiente hasta entregas con meses o incluso años de antelación. Esto permite a algunos compradores fijar los precios y reducir su exposición a las fluctuaciones a corto plazo. Los precios del día anterior, por ejemplo, reflejan el costo inmediato de la electricidad y dependen de factores como las condiciones meteorológicas, la producción de energías renovables y la demanda. Los contratos a más largo plazo también reflejan las expectativas respecto a factores más amplios, como los costes de los combustibles, la actividad económica y la disponibilidad de las centrales eléctricas. Los precios del gas en Europa se han triplicado con respecto a hace un año, ya que la guerra en Oriente Medio ha reducido el suministro mundial y ha intensificado la competencia con Asia. Esto también hace subir los costos de la electricidad, ya que las centrales de gas suelen marcar el precio mayorista de la electricidad cuando las fuentes más baratas no pueden producir lo suficiente para satisfacer la demanda. Los precios siguen estando muy por debajo de los picos extremos alcanzados durante la crisis de 2022, cuando Europa se apresuró a sustituir el gas ruso. La preocupación en esta ocasión no se centra tanto en los picos extremos de precios como en la perspectiva de que los costes elevados persistan durante todo el invierno. Parte del impacto queda oculto por el momento. Decenas de millones de hogares están protegidos por tarifas fijas o reguladas, mientras que muchos grandes usuarios industriales compran electricidad con meses o incluso años de antelación. Sin embargo, esos amortiguadores tienen una fecha de caducidad, lo que significa que los precios elevados prolongados acabarán repercutiendo a medida que se renueven los contratos. El impacto ya está empezando a llegar a los consumidores. Algunos proveedores han subido los precios para 2027, incluido un incremento del 3,3% en la tarifa eléctrica doméstica de EnBW a partir de enero. La coalición alemana acordó esta semana introducir una rebaja del impuesto sobre la electricidad para el próximo año con el fin de amortiguar el aumento de los costos. En la vecina Polonia, el primer ministro Donald Tusk declaró el martes que el país tiene previsto proteger a los consumidores de los altos precios. Y la presión podría agravarse considerablemente a medida que Europa se adentra en el invierno. En un escenario más grave, los contratos mensuales de electricidad podrían dispararse hasta los €300 si los precios del gas siguen subiendo y la región sufre otra ola de frío inusual, según BB Energy Trading Ltd. Incluso a los precios actuales, la presión se está extendiendo. Dos proveedores de electricidad alemanes, Grüüün y Stromee, han dejado de suministrar electricidad a sus clientes, repitiendo la crisis de 2022, cuando decenas de pequeños proveedores de electricidad y gas quebraron tras verse sorprendidos por unos precios al por mayor sin precedentes. Otros también se están viendo en apuros. En Austria, la empresa de servicios públicos Verbund AG afirmó que la escasa producción hidroeléctrica la obligó a comprar electricidad a precios elevados en el mercado al contado, lo que supuso un impacto de 120 millones de euros en sus resultados durante los primeros nueve meses del año. El fabricante español de acero inoxidable Acerinox señaló que el aumento de los costes energéticos afectó negativamente a sus operaciones en Europa en €16 millones durante el último trimestre. Los contratos de compra a largo plazo solo cubrían aproximadamente la mitad de su demanda de electricidad, según un informe de resultados. La razón por la que Feralpi no ha cubierto gran parte de sus compras de electricidad es que muchos de sus clientes realizan pedidos con poca antelación. Las empresas que carecen de coberturas suficientes “correrán el riesgo de operar con pérdidas, lo que les obligará a plantearse paros de producción, al menos parciales”, este invierno, afirmó Timothée de Rancourt, director de la consultora Royale Energy Solutions, con sede en París. A precios extremos, la electricidad puede llegar a ser más valiosa para algunas empresas industriales que los productos que fabrican con ella. Las empresas que fijaron el precio de la electricidad a niveles mucho más bajos están revendiendo al mercado parte de esos volúmenes cubiertos, en lugar de utilizar la electricidad para mantener las fábricas en funcionamiento, señaló De Rancourt. Las energías renovables han ayudado a amortiguar el impacto del aumento de los costes energéticos. Durante el verano y principios de otoño, la generación solar récord coincidió con una demanda de electricidad relativamente baja. Sin embargo, a medida que la producción solar disminuye y el consumo aumenta de cara al invierno, Europa depende en mayor medida de la energía eólica —una fuente de suministro más volátil que puede reducirse drásticamente durante períodos prolongados de tiempo sin viento—. El creciente riesgo invernal está llevando a los gobiernos a preparar medidas de respaldo adicionales. Alemania se está preparando para volver a poner en funcionamiento centrales eléctricas de carbón y petróleo que actualmente se mantienen en la reserva de la red, en caso de que se produzca una emergencia de gas natural este invierno, según un proyecto de ley al que ha tenido acceso Bloomberg News. Los precios alemanes del mercado diario se situaron por encima de los €300 en tres ocasiones durante las últimas dos semanas, mientras que en algunos cuartos de hora se superaron los €600, ya que las condiciones de “Dunkelflaute” —días calmos y nublados— frenaron la generación de energías renovables. Se han producido subidas de precios similares en todo el continente y en el Reino Unido. En el caso de los hogares, los costes mayoristas de la electricidad suelen repercutir con cierto retraso debido a los contratos fijos, las operaciones de cobertura de las empresas de suministro, las tarifas reguladas y las medidas de protección del Gobierno. Estas disposiciones varían considerablemente en toda Europa, lo que significa que los consumidores notarán el impacto a ritmos diferentes. En el Reino Unido, el límite máximo del precio de la energía se disparará en enero, y se prevé que la factura media anual aumente un 26%, hasta alcanzar las 2.166 libras, según Cornwall Insight Ltd. En Alemania, el precio medio de las diez tarifas eléctricas más baratas ha aumentado alrededor de un 33% desde antes del estallido de la guerra de Irán, hasta situarse en 34,6 céntimos por kilovatio-hora, según el portal comparativo Verivox. “Esperamos nuevas subidas de precios”, afirmó el experto en energía Thorsten Storck.

Nov 21 : FIFPRO said on Saturday it was "deeply concerned" by public comments from Bayern Munich's leadership about Jamal Musiala's contract, accusing the German champions of putting pressure on the midfielder while he recovers from health problems. The global players' union was responding to recent remarks by senior Bayern officials, including honorary president Uli Hoeness, CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen and supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, about Musiala's future at the club. Hoeness earlier this month questioned whether the 23-year-old Germany international could return to his previous level after being diagnosed with a neurological disorder. Dreesen later backed those remarks, saying Bayern would evaluate Musiala's progress and discuss his future with his representatives.

Rummenigge subsequently defended the comments, saying the club's consideration of Musiala's health and contract situation was both responsible and normal. "Bayern's honorary president, chief executive and former chief executive have all publicly questioned Musiala's contract in quick succession," FIFPRO said in a statement. "In FIFPRO's view, this is a coordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern's standing should know better." RUN OF INJURIES Musiala signed a contract extension with Bayern until 2030 in February last year. He has endured a difficult run of injuries and health setbacks in recent months. He broke his leg at the Club World Cup in July 2025, missed half of last season and collapsed twice within a few days in August before being diagnosed with a neurological disorder. In September, he suffered a hamstring injury. "Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala. Across professional football, uncertainty about a player's future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury," FIFPRO added. "Making Musiala's health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure. Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives. "FIFPRO stands with Jamal Musiala and with all players who honour their commitments. We expect their employers to do the same." Dreesen rejected suggestions that Bayern were trying to pressure Musiala. "We all hope that Jamal will be the Jamal we know again," Dreesen said on Saturday. "He needs time to come back. We've said that several times now. He has to be given that time. And then we'll see how things look at the beginning of next year." Dreesen added that there was no need to keep talking about Musiala's contract. After September's injury, Musiala returned as a substitute in Bayern's 1-1 home draw with Cologne in the Bundesliga on Friday.

Source: Reuters

ROME, Nov 21 : Lazio continued to prove their Serie A title credentials with a comfortable 3-0 home win over Lecce on Saturday, as Gennaro Gattuso's side remained unbeaten this season and extended their lead at the top of the standings. Tijjani Noslin scored in each half and Davide Frattesi wrapped up the win in style with a 90th-minute strike as Lazio earned their 10th victory in 12 games to move to 32 points, four ahead of Inter Milan who travel to Atlanta on Sunday. Como are fourth on 26 points following a 2-0 win over Cagliari thanks to goals from Jacobo Ramon and Lucas da Cunha. The majority of Lazio fans continue to boycott home matches in protest against club owner Claudio Lotito, yet the unrest has done little to unsettle Gattuso's men.

"I look at it the other way around," Frattesi told DAZN when asked about being top of the league. "We're on 32 points, with eight still to go (for 40 points which usually guarantees survival)." Lazio took the lead in the 25th minute when Gustav Isaksen floated a cross into the area where Noslin rose above his marker to steer his header into the bottom corner. Noslin's second came from a delightful back-heeled pass from Kenneth Taylor which the Lazio striker rifled into the net and the hosts finished the game with a quick counter. Matteo Cancellieri's header put Frattesi through and he sent a deft lob over the keeper from the edge of the area. "I saw the keeper come out and did the first thing that came to mind," Frattesi said. Frattesi, who joined in August on-loan from Inter, continues to prove an inspired signing and after scoring in Lazio's opening three wins, has now netted for the second consecutive game.

Nov 21 : Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha fired his side to the top of the German Bundesliga table on Saturday as they won 1-0 at bottom side Borussia Moenchengladbach. Bayern Munich were held to a 1-1 draw at home by Cologne on Friday, with striker Harry Kane suffering a serious ankle injury, and Dortmund capitalised to take a two-point lead at the summit.  The home side played far better than their position at the bottom of the league would suggest, withstanding waves of tremendous pressure from the visitors, but they finally cracked in the 80th minute when Nmecha picked up the ball on the edge of a packed penalty area and let fly.  Unsighted by the thicket of bodies in front of him, Gladbach goalkeeper Daniel Batz misjudged the trajectory of the ball, and it flew over his right shoulder and into the net.

Gladbach created a number of chances, but keeper Gregor Kobel came to the rescue with fine saves for Dortmund, and once the goal went in, there was no way back for the hosts.  Dortmund have 24 points after 10 games, two ahead of Bayern and third-placed Freiburg, who beat Elversberg 1-0.  Fourth-placed RB Leipzig had five different players on the scoresheet in a 5-1 drubbing of Union Berlin that lifted them to 21 points. Bayer Leverkusen thumped four goals without reply past Paderborn to remain fifth.  Eintracht Frankfurt remained in the running for the European places thanks to a 1-0 win over Hoffenheim, with Jonathan Burkardt's first-half goal securing the victory.

EDINBURGH, Nov 21 : Loose-forward Liam McConnell and winger Darcy Graham each scored a hat-trick of tries as Scotland romped to a 67-5 victory over Japan in their final Nations Championship pool fixture at Murrayfield on Saturday. The home side ran in 11 tries as they had too much pace and power for Eddie Jones’ Japan, who were crushed 78-15 by England last weekend and have now lost all three games in November. Scotland are fourth in the Northern Hemisphere Nations Championship table with 20 points from five games, while Japan are fifth in the Southern Hemisphere pool. "This group was hungry for game time the past few weeks, there were some disappointed faces the last few weeks, but everyone was raring to go today," McConnell told the BBC.

FAST

LONDON, Nov 21 : England outclassed New Zealand 37-12 at Twickenham on Saturday as a record victory margin over the All Blacks and a bonus point gave them a chance of making next weekend's Nations Championship final. The hosts dominated the first half, Henry Slade going over inside five minutes before tries from Jack van Poortvliet and Ben Earl made it 19-0, but Ethan de Groot's try on the cusp of halftime gave the All Blacks hope. Ollie Chessum powered over for England shortly after the restart, however, and after New Zealand's Beauden Barrett marked his 150th cap with a superb try, Seb Atkinson coasted in to effectively end the contest just after the hour mark. Replacement flyhalf Marcus Smith kicked two late penalties to give England a 25-point winning margin, surpassing their 17-point victory over New Zealand in 2012.

"I love the way the team is growing and we look forward to the future," England captain Maro Itoje said. England moved top of the Northern Hemisphere table on 25 points and their superior points difference means France, on 21, realistically need a bonus-point win over Argentina later on Saturday to make next Sunday's final at Twickenham. New Zealand remained top of the Southern Hemisphere standings on 22 points, one ahead of South Africa who face Ireland on Saturday knowing a win would put them in the final. The defeat also marks only the third time, and second in the professional era, that New Zealand have lost five tests in a year, which last happened in 1998. "We're under pressure, we put ourselves under pressure, England put us under pressure and, when we had our opportunities, we either gave the ball away or made errors, so pretty disappointing," New Zealand hooker Codie Taylor said. ALL BLACKS SLUMP TO RECORD LOSS After last weekend's historic defeat by Wales, New Zealand reverted to a much stronger lineup and England had prepared to face a side with a point to prove. But the All Blacks barely got out of their own half before the break and remained in touching distance only because England failed to capitalise on their control. England – whose former captain Lewis Moody, who last year revealed he was diagnosed with motor neurone disease, joined the English players in facing the pre-match haka – took a deserved early lead when Slade ran on to a superb kick from Fin Smith. New Zealand clung on until the 32nd minute when Cadan Murley, a late replacement for Tommy Freeman, broke through the middle. Slade chased his own chip over the top and nearly scored, before van Poortvliet went over from close range. Four minutes before the break, Earl peeled away from the scrum and breezed past Cam Roigard, Fin Smith adding the conversion to give England a well-deserved 19-point lead. De Groot's try felt significant, the All Blacks converting their first real chance of the game to give themselves a foothold for an unlikely comeback. England, however, started the second half as sharply as the first, Chessum stealing a lineout before applying the finish touch. New Zealand hit back through Barrett, but England were unfazed and centre Atkinson's score ended the All Blacks' hopes of a comeback.

Source: Reuters

TURIN, Italy, Nov 21 : Seven-times Grand Slam champion Carlos Alcaraz battled back from a set down to beat American Ben Shelton 3-6 6-3 7-6(1) in their ATP Finals semi-final to charge into Sunday's showcase for the second consecutive year. Alcaraz, beaten by Shelton in the US Open quarter-finals on the Spaniard's return from a four-month injury break, stretched his winning run to 13 matches after back-to-back titles in Vienna and Paris. He will face either world number one Alexander Zverev or Daniil Medvedev of Russia, who meet later on Saturday. "I was a little bit frustrated at the beginning because I didn't start the match the way I wanted to," said Alcaraz, unbeaten on indoor courts this season.

"Just happy that I came back in the second set playing such great tennis, step by step, focused on all my things and ended up playing good tennis. The third set was even closer." Shelton, making his second consecutive appearance in the season finale, grabbed an early break to race to a 3-0 lead. Alcaraz, whose fitness had come under scrutiny after he left the court with heavy strapping on his left leg following Wednesday's win over Medvedev, had his thigh wrapped heavily against Shelton. He upped his game and started moving the American around more, engaging him in longer rallies. He earned two break points at 4-2 but could not convert either with Shelton's booming serve getting him out of trouble.  The world number four fired a second-serve ace on his first set point to move ahead but Alcaraz went 5-3 up in the second before serving out the second set. The pair traded blows in the third set before Alcaraz eased through the tiebreak, sealing the win with a return winner.

FAST

PORTIMAO, Portugal, Nov 21 : Marc Marquez's chance to clinch an eighth MotoGP title on Saturday ended in the gravel when the Ducati rider crashed out of third place on the penultimate lap of the Portuguese Grand Prix sprint which was won by Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi. Marquez had needed to outscore title rival Jorge Martin by just two points to be crowned champion on Saturday but the Ducati rider lost control on lap 11 as rain started to fall and he went out. Aprilia's Martin eventually finished fifth to reduce Marquez's lead to 55 points ahead of Sunday's race, where Marquez can still seal the title with a round to spare. "We have the big advantage (in points) luckily," Marquez said with a wry smile when speaking to TNT Sports.

"It was a very difficult sprint race, especially on that lap it started to rain more. When I arrived on that corner, I didn't realise that it was so wet. "It's true that the people want to celebrate as soon as possible but I'm calm. The good thing is that I'm perfect on the physical side, so tomorrow we will have another chance." Trackhouse rider Raul Fernandez finished second while Gresini Racing's Alex Marquez completed the podium. The crash also keeps alive Bezzecchi's very slim title hopes but the Italian remains 62 points adrift and will need Marquez to score no further points this season to stay in contention. "I'm so happy. The sprint has been like a torture for me till now, so very, very happy to make this kind of result," said Bezzecchi after his first sprint victory of the season. "Huge thanks to the team because they never stop believing in me... Now we continue working for tomorrow and we will try our best also in the longer race (on Sunday)." MARQUEZ EXERCISES CAUTION Bezzecchi had broken the lap record to snatch pole and the Italian had the perfect start off the line while Fernandez found a way past a cautious Marquez to move up to second. Bezzecchi and Fernandez peeled away at the front and Marquez seemed to be holding up the rest of the pack while his brother Alex moved up to fourth behind him, with Martin back in seventh despite his best efforts to overtake riders. Martin continued to look for openings and although he moved up to sixth when he overtook VR46 Racing's Fabio di Giannantonio, he could not find a way past KTM's Pedro Acosta, who will be Marquez's teammate at Ducati next season. However, light rain had started to fall across the track and Marc crashed out right in front of his brother Alex, sliding into the gravel as shocked spectators looked on in disbelief. "Everything was going really under control... But then we arrive at turn seven and suddenly it was this slight rain that caused him to crash," Alex said. "Then for three to four corners I was super slow because I don't want to crash!" Alex then kept Acosta at bay on the last lap to secure the final podium spot, finishing less than half a second ahead of the KTM rider.

Source: Reuters

FAST

MANCHESTER, England, Nov 21 : Manchester City's slide from top of the table to a club in crisis reached an uncomfortable new low on Saturday when a 1-1 draw with Fulham extended a run that would have been virtually unthinkable only weeks ago. A team who opened the season with seven straight Premier League victories have now followed up with four successive games without a win.  The numbers are piling up. City have lost three of their last four league games, as many defeats as they suffered in their previous 36. They have also gone nine games across all competitions without a clean sheet. And beyond the statistics, it was the mood at the Etihad Stadium that told the full story.

As Fulham celebrated ending a run of 20 consecutive defeats against City and taking a point from the league giants for the first time in 15 years, thousands of home supporters headed for the exits before the final whistle.  Those who remained among the otherwise huge swathes of empty blue seats greeted the final whistle with a chorus of boos.  Glum-faced City boss Enzo Maresca trudged down the tunnel. "Tough moment in terms of results... we were anxious in terms of going behind," said Maresca, who had changed the pre-game routine by having the squad stay at the new hotel on the Etihad campus on Friday night. "In this moment all we can try to do is recover and we have another big game here on Tuesday (against Napoli in the Champions League).  "We changed a bit at halftime the way we were pressing. Second half we were much better. We had so many moments where we could have made a better choice but it's important that we arrived there and created chances and soon we can score more goals." Their next league game is a trip to league leaders Arsenal and suddenly it looks less like a title showdown than a test of City's nerve. The frustration stemmed as much from the performance as the result. City looked flat and passive for long stretches, vulnerable whenever Fulham attacked and strangely lacking urgency in possession.  During one stretch, exasperated supporters groaned when Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno was repeatedly allowed to take his time on the ball without any pressure. The intensity that has defined recent City sides was absent. Elliot Anderson's equaliser in the 57th minute at least rescued a point but the midfielder acknowledged that the recurring pattern of City falling behind was becoming a concern. "It's very frustrating," he said. "Going a goal down wasn't ideal but it seems to be happening. The second half was better, more intensity, we pushed higher. We just struggled to get the second goal. "We're working on that. We are doing everything we can to fix it." Anderson struck a volley into the bottom corner for his first league goal for City since joining from Nottingham Forest in the close season.  "That's my job on the edge of the box on corners from that side," he said. "Try to get a clean connection on target. Trying to stay calm in those situations and make good contact." The 24-year-old said there was no sense of panic despite a turbulent period for the club, with City's worsening form coinciding with their appeal against more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules. City have denied any wrongdoing.

Source: Reuters

item.title: COP31: G77 accuses developed nations of dividing bloc, lack of transparency
item.description: Speaking to PTI, a G77 representative alleged that developed nations are "dividing the developing nations" and hindering the process for a finance roadmap.
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / COP31: G77 accuses developed nations of dividing bloc, lack of transparency

COP31: G77 accuses developed nations of dividing bloc, lack of transparency Speaking to PTI, a G77 representative alleged that developed nations are "dividing the developing nations" and hindering the process for a finance roadmap

A COP31 sign is displayed at the venue of the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkey. (Photo: Reuters)

Press Trust of India 2 min read Last Updated : Nov 21 2026 | 11:35 PM IST

Listen to This Article

With the UN Climate Change conference (COP31) running beyond its scheduled close, developing nations have raised concerns over transparency from the presidencies to address their demands in the final outcome document. Speaking to PTI, a G77 representative alleged that developed nations are "dividing the developing nations" and hindering the process for a finance roadmap. Group of 77 (G77) is a coalition of 134 developing countries plus China at the UN that promotes members' collective economic interests and strengthens their joint negotiating power. "G77 is being divided by the European Union and High-Ambition coalition (HAC), which is an informal group of developed and developing countries within the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).

Meanwhile, the presidencies have also not been transparent with us," the representative said, on the condition of anonymity. Also Read

COP31 climate talks extend into overtime amid deadlock on fossil fuels

COP31: India, developing nations challenge EU on climate finance

Our development goals must move alongside sustainable future: Yadav

Nepal seeks billions at COP31; $20 mn pledged for disaster survivors so far

Global electrification push stalls at COP31 amid opposition from nations

They alleged that when the G77 called a meeting with the presidency seeking transparency on finance on Saturday, no clear answer was given to them, but they were called for consultation in groups and sub-groups selectively later. "G77 called a meeting with the COP31 presidency asking for transparency on finance, but no clear answer was given. We are concerned that what the developing nations haven't agreed to will be parachuted in the final text," the G77 official said. Expressing concerns over multiple developing nations' ministers travelling back to their home countries due to the summit running overtime, the official said, "there is a question on whether the final decision will be taken on consensus."   They further alleged that there is a lack of political will from developed nations to help developing nations combat climate change, and that the delay was a "pre-planned tactic."   The COP31 Presidency is held by Turkiye, with Murat Kurum serving as COP31 President, whereas Australia's Chris Bowen is serving as the summit's President of Negotiations.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)
